newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-GKN sees scope for further growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-GKN sees scope for further growth.

text.p: International engineering group GKN Plc said after reporting a strong rise in half-year profits on Wednesday that it saw plenty of scope for more growth from all areas, including its traditional mainstay, the vehicle driveshaft business.
Pre-tax profits for the six months to June 28 rose to 203 million pounds from 181 million last year, topping market forecasts of between 185 and 193 million pounds.

The firm said sterling's strength in translating results belied stronger underlying growth which would have shown a 25 percent jump in profits at constant exchange rates on a six percent rise in sales.

Chief executive CK Chow said a strategic review of the business undertaken since he took over the reins in January had identified three areas of organic growth and a further three "platforms for growth" following recent acquisitions.
Areas promising most organic growth are the driveshaft business, the Chep distribution pallets business and Westland Helicopters.
Despite the maturity of the West European and North American vehicle markets and GKN's leading market share the company believed there was still rich potential for growth, he said.
GKN was taking new supply contracts as vehicle manufacturers decided to outsource more components and it was also moving in on emerging markets, particularly in China and Mexico.
"It is our aim to triple our business in emerging markets in the next five years," Chow said.

The automotive products division made an operating profit of 106 million pounds on sales of 1,019 million pounds in the six months to June 28, improving the operating margin by one percentage point to 10.4 percent.
"And that (margin) is sustainable because of our continuous productivity improvement programme," he said.

In addition, he said, the automotive markets also gave GKN one of its three "platforms for growth," as GKN's business making engineered components by moulding powdered metals is set to take off following its takeover of U.S. firm Sinter Metals for $570 million in May.
Seventy percent of the market was in automotive components, with potential for over 200 components per vehicle being made from powdered metal.
"In one step it has made us the world's largest supplier in precision powder metal parts and its a fast-growing market," he said.
Now GKN was on the lookout for further acquisitions in the sintering business, but declined to comment on recent speculation GKN might have its eye on British rival T&N.

"The sector is growing at six to 10 percent a year and we believe we can grow faster than that because we can play the consolidator role," he said. "It is both organic growth and we will also acquire more companies in the future."

Chow said he had also identified a second platform for growth in automotive components in GKN's 'Agritechnical' business supplying off-road vehicle components, which led to the acquisition of a stake in Italian firm Agrindustrial in March.

Meanwhile he said GKN's Industrial Services division centring on its Chep goods distribution pallet hire business was also set to grow through a combination of geographic expansion, increased market share and product innovation.

The division made an operating profit of 42 million pounds in the first half of this year on sales of 208 million pounds but Chow said profits grew 31 percent at constant exchange rates and its pallet pools were growing at 20 percent a year.
In the aerospace and defence business Chow said helicopter production at its Westland subsidiary was also set to take off, fuelled by an order book currently worth 3.8 billion pounds.

Helicopter production rates are due to rise from nine a year in 1997 and 1998 to 27 in 1999 and 42 in the year 2000, he said. Further sales this year include orders from the Italian navy for 16 EH101s and from South Korea for 13 Lynx helicopters.
Separately GKN Westland Aerospace, which makes substructures for other aircraft manufacturers, was enjoying strong organic growth from the recent industry upturn.
Chow said he now saw Westland Aerospace as its third platform for growth having added three more acquisitions to the business in the first half of this year.

In the first half of the year, operating profits at the Aerospace and Special Vehicles division, which includes its GKN Defence armoured cars business, jumped to 51 million pounds from 38 million last time, on sales of 460 million pounds.
GKN said Westland made a strong contribution with profits growth in all its activities, while GKN Defence "performed steadily."
-- Greg Mahlich, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
